proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 e_{p,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
We first establish the simultaneous mass event.  If \(Z\) is any random variable supported on \([0,1]\), define
\(\psi(\lambda)=\log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\).  Under exponential tilting by \(e^{\lambda Z}\), differentiation under the expectation is valid because \(Z\) is bounded, and
\[
 \psi''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)
 \le E_{\lambda}\bigl[(Z-1/2)^2\bigr]\le\frac14.
\]
Since \(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\), integrating this inequality twice gives
\[
 \log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},
 \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For fixed \(x\in\mathcal X\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes
\(\widehat p_x=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\) the average of independent Bernoulli variables with common mean \(p_x\).  Applying exponential Markov inequality to (1) and minimizing the upper-tail exponent
\(-n\lambda e_{p,n}+n\lambda^2/8\) at \(\lambda=4e_{p,n}\), and applying the same argument to the lower tail, yields
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \bigl(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>e_{p,n}\bigr)
 \le 2e^{-2ne_{p,n}^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.                           \tag{2}
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives, uniformly in \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le e_{p,n}\right)
 \ge1-\frac{\alpha}{3}.                                             \tag{3}
\]
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the vector \((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) is nonnegative and sums to one.  Thus \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\) says that the event in (3) is precisely
\(\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\), and the claimed coordinate bound holds on that event.

We next prove the regular-count inequality.  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p)\), then for every \(t>0\), exponential Markov inequality and \(1+v\le e^v\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr(N\le np/2)
 &\le e^{tnp/2}E[e^{-tN}]\\
 &=e^{tnp/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^n\\
 &\le\exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{4}
\]
Taking \(t=\log2\) in (4), and using \((1-\log2)/2\ge1/8\), gives
\[
 \Pr(N\le np/2)\le e^{-np(1-\log2)/2}\le e^{-np/8}.                \tag{5}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\).  Consequently
\(\{n_x<np_{\min}/2\}\subseteq\{n_x<np_x/2\}\), and a union bound applied to (5) proves
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 \le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.                                           \tag{6}
\]

It remains to control mass profiling.  Let \(p=(p_x)_x\) and \(p'=(p'_x)_x\) lie in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and fix \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) for every \(x\).  Put
\[
 e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}.
\]
The continuum constraints in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\) give, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2>0,
 \qquad |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)+e_n.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Division in the next display is therefore justified by (7).  By
\(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\),
\[
 \left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 \le B_Y+\frac{e_n}{f_x(a)}
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                            \tag{8}
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) gives
\(|p_x-p'_x|\le|p_x-\widehat p_x|+|p'_x-\widehat p_x|\le2e_{p,n}\).
Hence the triangle inequality and (8) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
 \right|
 &\le\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}|p_x-p'_x|
       \sup_{a\in I}\left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|\\
 &\le2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}.                 \tag{9}
 \end{aligned}
\]

Finally, let \(\gamma=\beta-1/2\).  The enlarged declared range \(\beta>1/2\) gives exactly \(\gamma>0\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\),
\[
 K_n\sim\frac{\log n}{\log\log n},
\]
and \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\) gives
\[
 b_{\mu,n}
 =4\kappa^{-1}C_{\beta,\mathcal A}(R_q+B_YR_f)K_n^{-\gamma}
 =O(r_n),                                                            \tag{10}
\]
because \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^\gamma\).  Moreover,
\[
 \log\left(\frac{e_{p,n}}{r_n}\right)
 =-\frac12\log n+\gamma\log\log n+O(\log\log\log n)
 \longrightarrow-\infty,                                          \tag{11}
\]
where \(m\), \(\alpha\), and \(\gamma\) are fixed.  Thus \(e_{p,n}=o(r_n)\).  Combining this with (10) gives
\[
 2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}=o(r_n),               \tag{12}
\]
which, together with (3), (6), and (9), proves every assertion.

proposed.comparator_claim: Our contributions include establishing identifiability without any assumption on the noise except for coordinate independence.
We identify the average dose-response function for a continuously valued error contaminated treatment by a weighted conditional expectation.
Uniform confidence bands in deconvolution with unknown error distribution.
We establish asymptotic validity of the proposed confidence band.
This paper proposes an inference method based on Kotlarski's identity.
We show that expected diameters and coverage properties of resulting sets have uniform validity over a large class of models.
An inequality is given for the expected length of a confidence interval given that a particular distribution generated the data.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The enlarged class removes the separately assumed local spectral-modulus restriction, but it still does not literally match any comparator's causal experiment or inferential promise; the conservative unmatched positioning is therefore retained explicitly in the synchronized post-image.

prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. The fixed quantitative class allows every \(\beta>1/2\) and every fixed \(q_e>1\); its error-moment radius itself yields a uniform protected neighborhood, so no separate local spectral-modulus restriction is assumed. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. Two simultaneous bands are separated sharply: an explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve construction is uniformly honest and clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), while an abstract noncomputational exact-class construction is uniformly honest with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. Neither construction proves the candidate \(r_n\) rate. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus remains unresolved, so there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a shrinking uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band for blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets. In the present class, a fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius yields local nonvanishing automatically, but the empirical-grid outer set still lacks a quantitative marked inverse modulus, and the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band converse remains unproved.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem over compactly supported \(H^\beta\) signal and marked channels for every \(\beta>1/2\). Compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, and the first moment implied by \(q_e>1\) gives the uniform bound \(|\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\), hence the derived protected pair \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\). The causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve. The distinction between qualitative identification and quantitative confidence-set diameter is essential here.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers two inference maps on the enlarged class. The explicit map uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves; error sieves protected on the moment-derived neighborhood; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. It proves uniform simultaneous coverage and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), but no shrinkage. In parallel, exact empirical-channel residuals are profiled over a compact projected nuisance class with \(\beta>1/2\), \(q_e>1\), and no separate spectral-modulus constraint. Compactness, expanding-grid equality, and marked cocycle injectivity prove that this abstract exact-class band is uniformly honest and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. The qualitative argument supplies no explicit modulus, and the sharp \(O(r_n)\) upper and matching marked converse remain open.

sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps; only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location. For a fixed \(q_e>1\), their common \(q_e\)-moment radius is at most \(M_e\). This moment bound implies \(|\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\), so local spectral protection is derived rather than separately imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The explicit conservative procedure uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), valid uniformly over the full range \(\beta>1/2\), finite atomic characteristic-function families for the two errors using the moment-derived protected neighborhood, and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); its outer splines are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. A second, abstract procedure profiles the same empirical radii with no approximation allowances over the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\), then takes clipped extrema of \(\mu_{\vartheta}\). The latter is an infinite-dimensional existence construction and is not claimed to be computationally implementable.

prose_updates.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery. Their qualitative identification model requires no common error-moment radius and identifies only up to translation. This paper instead fixes a \(q_e>1\) moment radius for uniform inference and centers the second error; unlike the earlier version, it imposes no separate local spectral-modulus restriction because \(|\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\) supplies a protected neighborhood. Their rate argument uses a protected-region integrated contrast with nearly parametric forward error and does not supply a Lipschitz inverse for the present grid set whose tolerance already contains polynomial Jackson error. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not establish a shrinking marked-quotient band here. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None of these sources proves the missing quantitative diameter for the current empirical-grid outer set.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, the Jackson outer-sieve embedding for every \(\beta>1/2\), moment-derived local nonvanishing for every fixed \(q_e>1\), and clipped uniform coverage are proved. The finite grid-sieve set has no quantitative inverse modulus and therefore no shrinking-width guarantee. Exact-class compactness yields a separate uniformly honest band with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected width, but gives no rate, tuning law, or finite algorithm. The sharp-rate program still requires a protected-cube analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the lower-side obstruction; only its former obstruction tied to a separately fixed \(c_0\) disappears.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model fixes compact dose support, bounded outcomes, finite-stratum masses, overlap, Sobolev radii with \(\beta>1/2\), an error-moment radius at a fixed \(q_e>1\), centering of the second replicate error, and the structural causal response surface. It does not impose a separate local spectral-modulus restriction: the moment radius gives the uniform derived neighborhood \(|t|\le(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) with modulus at least \(1/2\). The explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\), with no proved shrinkage. The parallel exact-class band is abstract and noncomputational; it is uniformly honest and its expected maximal width is uniformly \(o(1)\), but no explicit rate follows. In particular, no \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or rate-elbow claim is made. The matching-converse kernel remains open as \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\), after removal of only its obsolete separately fixed-modulus obstruction.

statement_notes.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage and proves that mass uncertainty is negligible at the candidate scale \(r_n\) throughout the enlarged range \(\beta>1/2\); it does not assert a shrinking total band diameter.

proposed.statement:
Under the relaxed outer-sieve construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there are splines \(\widetilde f_{x,n}\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(\widetilde q_{x,n}\in\mathscr Q_n(\widetilde f_{x,n})\) such that
\[
 \|\widetilde f_{x,n}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{f,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde q_{x,n}-q_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{q,n}.
\]
With the true masses \((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\), their profiled ADRF satisfies
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}-\mu(a)
 \right|
 \le 2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})
 \le b_{\mu,n}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but its proof spine now explicitly depends on the proved Jackson lemma valid throughout the enlarged range \(\beta>1/2\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and an \(n\) for which the
deterministic tuning objects are defined.  We use the corrected class with
\(q_e>1\), and no separately assumed local spectral modulus.  Define
\[
 U_j^H=\max\{-H_n,\min\{U_j,H_n\}\}.
\]
On \(\{|U_j|>H_n\}\), one has
\(1\le |U_j|^{q_e}H_n^{-q_e}\).  Therefore
\(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\) gives
\[
 P(|U_j|>H_n)
 \le H_n^{-q_e}E_P|U_j|^{q_e}
 \le M_eH_n^{-q_e}.                                                \tag{1}
\]
Because \(U_j^H=U_j\) off this tail event and two complex numbers of unit
modulus are at distance at most two, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|E_Pe^{itU_j^H}-\phi_j(t)\right|
 &\le E_P\left|e^{itU_j^H}-e^{itU_j}\right|\\
 &\le2P(|U_j|>H_n)
 \le2M_eH_n^{-q_e}=\tau_{e,n}.                                    \tag{2}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Clipping cannot increase absolute value, so
\[
 E_P|U_j^H|^{q_e}\le E_P|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e.                       \tag{3}
\]

For \(j=2\), the first absolute moment exists by
\(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}local\text{-}modulus}\)
applied to the law of \(U_2\).  Thus the centering identity in
\(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) may be subtracted from the clipped
mean.  Since \(q_e>1\), on \(\{|U_2|>H_n\}\) we have
\(|U_2|\le H_n^{1-q_e}|U_2|^{q_e}\), and hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |E_PU_2^H|
 &=|E_P(U_2^H-U_2)|\\
 &\le E_P\{|U_2|\mathbf 1(|U_2|>H_n)\}\\
 &\le H_n^{1-q_e}E_P|U_2|^{q_e}
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                              \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is the only step of the atomic embedding that uses the strict threshold
\(q_e>1\); it also shows why the centering constraint contracts as
\(H_n\to\infty\).

We next replace the law of \(U_j^H\), supported on \([-H_n,H_n]\), by an
atomic law preserving all grid values and the two moments needed above.  Put
\[
 D=2|\Gamma_n|+2
\]
and define the continuous map
\[
 v(u)=\left(
   (\operatorname{Re}e^{itu},\operatorname{Im}e^{itu})_{t\in\Gamma_n},
   u,|u|^{q_e}
 \right)\in\mathbb R^D.                                           \tag{5}
\]
Finite-valued approximations to \(U_j^H\) have expectations under \(v\) in
the convex hull of \(v([-H_n,H_n])\), and uniform continuity of \(v\) on
this compact interval makes those expectations converge to
\(E_Pv(U_j^H)\).  Thus the latter vector initially lies in the closure of
that convex hull.

We now prove that this convex hull is closed while simultaneously obtaining
the required support bound.  Suppose any finite convex representation uses
more than \(D+1\) locations \(u_r\), with weights \(w_r\).
Then the augmented vectors \((1,v(u_r))\in\mathbb R^{D+1}\) are linearly
dependent.  Thus there are real numbers \(a_r\), not all zero, such that
\[
 \sum_r a_r=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_r a_rv(u_r)=0.                                               \tag{6}
\]
After replacing every \(a_r\) by \(-a_r\) if necessary, at least one
\(a_r\) is positive.  With
\[
 c=\min_{r:a_r>0}\frac{w_r}{a_r}>0,
 \qquad
 w'_r=w_r-ca_r,
\]
equation (6) shows that \((w'_r)_r\) has the same total mass and barycenter,
all its entries are nonnegative, and at least one positive-weight location is
removed.  Repetition leaves at most
\[
 D+1=2|\Gamma_n|+3\le M_n                                         \tag{7}
\]
locations, where the last inequality is the definition
\(M_n=2|\Gamma_n|+4\).  It follows that the whole convex hull is the image of
the compact set consisting of the \(D\)-simplex of weights and
\((D+1)\) copies of \([-H_n,H_n]\) under the continuous barycenter map.
The convex hull is therefore compact and hence closed.  The preceding limit
argument now proves that \(E_Pv(U_j^H)\) belongs to the convex hull, and (7)
provides a representation of it using at most \(D+1\) locations.

Let \(\bar Q_{j,n}\) be the resulting atomic law.  Order its locations and
pad the representation with zero-weight atoms at \(H_n\).  By (5), its
characteristic function \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\) agrees with the characteristic
function of \(U_j^H\) at every \(t\in\Gamma_n\), its mean agrees with
\(E_PU_j^H\), its support is contained in \([-H_n,H_n]\), and
\[
 \int |u|^{q_e}\,d\bar Q_{j,n}(u)
 =E_P|U_j^H|^{q_e}\le M_e.                                        \tag{8}
\]
Combining this exact grid agreement with (2) proves
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}
 |\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|
 \le\tau_{e,n}.                                                    \tag{9}
\]
For \(j=2\), exact preservation of the mean and (4) give
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}
 \le2M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                              \tag{10}
\]

It remains only to verify the protected-frequency clause of the corrected
\(\mathrm{def{:}error\text{-}sieves}\).  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}local\text{-}modulus}\) to
the probability law \(\bar Q_{j,n}\), using (8).  It yields directly
\[
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)|
 \ge c_*\ge c_*/2.                                                 \tag{11}
\]
Thus no grid interpolation and no independent spectral assumption are
needed.  Equations (8) and (11), together with the support and ordered-atom
construction, show
\(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\widetilde\Phi_{j,n}\).  In the second coordinate,
(10) verifies the additional centering tolerance, so
\(\bar\phi_{2,n}\in\Phi_{2,n}\); in the first coordinate,
\(\Phi_{1,n}=\widetilde\Phi_{1,n}\).  Equation (9) proves the displayed
grid approximation, and the first inequality in (10) is the stronger
representing-mean conclusion claimed by the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(j\in\{1,2\}\), let \(Q_j\) be a Borel probability law on
\(\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|u|^{q_e}\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e,
 \qquad
 \phi_{Q_j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{itu}\,dQ_j(u).
\]
Then
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|u|\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e^{1/q_e},
 \qquad
 |\phi_{Q_j}(s)-\phi_{Q_j}(t)|
 \le M_e^{1/q_e}|s-t|,
\]
and
\[
 |\phi_{Q_j}(t)|\ge 1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
Consequently, for the derived constants
\(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\),
\[
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\phi_{Q_j}(t)|\ge c_*.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because the corrected symbol range is \(q_e>1\), the conjugate exponent
\(q_e/(q_e-1)\) is finite.  H\"older's inequality with respect to the
probability measure \(Q_j\) gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|u|\,dQ_j(u)
 \le
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}|u|^{q_e}\,dQ_j(u)\right\}^{1/q_e}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}1\,dQ_j(u)\right\}^{1-1/q_e}
 \le M_e^{1/q_e}.                                                  \tag{1}
\]
For real \(v\), the fundamental theorem of calculus applied to
\(r\mapsto e^{irv}\) gives \(|e^{iv}-1|\le |v|\).  Hence, for all
\(s,t\in\mathbb R\), (1) and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\phi_{Q_j}(s)-\phi_{Q_j}(t)|
 &\le\int_{\mathbb R}|e^{isu}-e^{itu}|\,dQ_j(u)\\
 &\le |s-t|\int_{\mathbb R}|u|\,dQ_j(u)
 \le M_e^{1/q_e}|s-t|.                                            \tag{2}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(s=t\) is not useful for the lower bound; instead use
\(\phi_{Q_j}(0)=1\), the reverse triangle inequality, and the same pointwise
bound to obtain
\[
 |\phi_{Q_j}(t)|
 \ge 1-|\phi_{Q_j}(t)-\phi_{Q_j}(0)|
 \ge 1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}.                                            \tag{3}
\]
The positivity of \(M_e\) makes
\(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}>0\).  If \(|t|\le\nu_*\), then (3) yields
\[
 |\phi_{Q_j}(t)|
 \ge 1-\nu_*M_e^{1/q_e}
 =\frac12=c_*.
\]
This proves every assertion.

proposed.construction:
For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), let
\[
 \widetilde\Phi_{j,n}
 =\left\{
 t\longmapsto\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{j\ell}e^{itu_{j\ell}}:
 \begin{array}{l}
 w_{j\ell}\ge0,\quad \sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{j\ell}=1,\\
 -H_n\le u_{j1}\le\cdots\le u_{jM_n}\le H_n,\\
 \sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{j\ell}|u_{j\ell}|^{q_e}\le M_e,\\
 \displaystyle
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{j\ell}e^{itu_{j\ell}}\right|
 \ge c_*/2
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]
Set \(\Phi_{1,n}=\widetilde\Phi_{1,n}\) and
\[
 \Phi_{2,n}
 =\left\{\phi\in\widetilde\Phi_{2,n}:
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le2M_eH_n^{1-q_e}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\) are derived from
the common moment radius rather than separately imposed class indices.
Zero-weight atoms are placed at \(H_n\), and the ordered atom vector is
selected lexicographically, which removes representation ambiguity without
centering \(U_1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The error sieves now use the protected neighborhood and modulus derived from the moment radius, eliminating the old independently fixed spectral indices while retaining the compact atomic parametrization and approximate centering constraint.

proposed.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and all sufficiently
large \(n\), there is \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\Phi_{j,n}\) such that
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|\le\tau_{e,n}.
\]
For \(j=2\), its representing atomic law also satisfies
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but its proof now derives protected nonvanishing from the moment radius and therefore removes the separate local-modulus assumption from its proof spine.

proofs.proof_tex:
Throughout, the class is the corrected class in
\(\textnormal{def:exact-projected-class}\): \(\beta>1/2\), \(q_e>1\), and
there is no separately assumed spectral-modulus condition.  We first prove
compactness of the signal coordinates.  Use the Fourier convention
\[
 \|g\|_{H^\beta}^2
 =\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta
       |\widehat g(t)|^2\,dt.
 \tag{1}
\]
For every \(g\in H^\beta(\mathbb R)\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat g(t)|\,dt
 \le
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta|\widehat g(t)|^2\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}<\infty,
 \tag{2}
\]
where the last integral is finite exactly because \(\beta>1/2\).  Fourier
inversion therefore supplies a continuous representative and, again by
Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 |g(a)|
 \le \frac{\|g\|_{H^\beta}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
       \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2},
 \tag{3}
\]
as well as
\[
 |g(a)-g(b)|
 \le \frac{\|g\|_{H^\beta}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}|e^{-ita}-e^{-itb}|^2
                 (1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The integral in (4) tends to zero as \(|a-b|\to0\): its integrand converges
pointwise to zero and is dominated by the integrable function
\(4(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\).  Hence every fixed-radius \(H^\beta\)-ball is
uniformly bounded and has a common modulus of continuity on \(\mathcal A\).

For completeness, these two bounds give total boundedness directly.  Given
\(\epsilon>0\), choose a finite spatial mesh of \(\mathcal A\) so that the
common modulus in (4) is at most \(\epsilon/3\), and quantize the bounded
function values at the mesh points in increments at most \(\epsilon/3\).
Only finitely many quantized arrays occur.  If two functions have the same
array, comparison through a nearest mesh point bounds their uniform distance
by \(\epsilon\).  Selecting one representative of every nonempty array gives
a finite uniform \(\epsilon\)-net.

We next prove closedness of the fixed-support Sobolev ball in the uniform
topology.  Suppose that \(g_m\) is supported in \(\mathcal A\),
\(\|g_m\|_{H^\beta}\le R\), and \(g_m\to g\) uniformly on \(\mathcal A\).
The continuous representatives vanish at the boundary of \(\mathcal A\), so
their zero extensions satisfy
\[
 \|g_m-g\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)}
 \le (2B_A)^{1/2}\|g_m-g\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{5}
\]
Set \(h_m(t)=(1+t^2)^{\beta/2}\widehat g_m(t)\).  By (1), \((h_m)\) is
bounded in \(L^2(\mathbb R)\).  Expanding in a countable orthonormal basis and
diagonalizing yields a subsequence \(h_{m_k}\) and an \(h\in L^2\) such that
\(h_{m_k}\rightharpoonup h\) and
\[
 \|h\|_2\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|h_{m_k}\|_2.
 \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, coordinatewise convergence on the basis defines a bounded linear
functional first on finite linear combinations; the common norm bound extends
it to all of \(L^2\), and its representing coefficient sequence is \(h\).
By (5) and the Fourier isometry,
\(\widehat g_{m_k}\to\widehat g\) strongly in \(L^2\).  Multiplication by
\((1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}\) is bounded on \(L^2\), so the same sequence converges
weakly to \((1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}h\).  Uniqueness of the weak limit gives
\[
 \widehat g(t)=(1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}h(t),
 \qquad \|g\|_{H^\beta}\le R.
 \tag{7}
\]
Thus the fixed-support ball is closed.  Its total boundedness and closedness
show that it is compact: a Cauchy sequence converges uniformly, while repeated
selection from nested finite \(2^{-k}\)-nets gives a Cauchy subsequence of
every sequence.

Apply this argument with \(R=R_f\) and \(R=R_q\).  Uniform convergence on
the common support preserves nonnegativity and the pointwise inequalities, and
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}(f_m-f)(a)\,da\right|
 \le 2B_A\|f_m-f\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\longrightarrow0
 \tag{8}
\]
preserves normalization.  It also preserves \(f_x\ge\kappa\) on \(I\) and
\(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\).  Hence the joint signal subset in \(\mathscr K\) is a
closed subset of a finite product of compact spaces.  The mass vectors form a
closed subset of the finite-dimensional simplex because \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\)
and \(\sum_xp_x=1\).  Both coordinate blocks are therefore compact.

We now treat an error-law coordinate.  Let \((Q_m)\) satisfy the common
\(q_e\)-moment bound.  Since
\(\mathbf 1\{|u|>R\}\le |u|^{q_e}R^{-q_e}\),
\[
 \sup_m Q_m(|u|>R)\le M_eR^{-q_e}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Diagonal selection of the distribution functions at rational arguments,
followed by right-continuous regularization of the monotone pointwise limit,
therefore produces a distribution function \(F\): (9) forces its limits at
minus and plus infinity to be zero and one.  Let \(Q\) be its probability
law.  Rational bracketing gives convergence of the selected distribution
functions at every continuity point of \(F\).  To verify weak convergence
without any additional assumption, first use (9) to restrict a bounded
continuous test function to \([-R,R]\), then partition that interval at
continuity points of \(F\).  Upper and lower step-function bounds, uniform
continuity on \([-R,R]\), refinement of the partition, and finally
\(R\to\infty\) give
\[
 \int h\,dQ_m\longrightarrow\int h\,dQ
 \quad\text{for every bounded continuous }h.
 \tag{10}
\]
For every \(L<\infty\), the function \(|u|^{q_e}\wedge L\) is bounded and
continuous.  Thus (10) and monotone convergence imply
\[
 \int |u|^{q_e}\,dQ(u)
 =\sup_{L<\infty}\int (|u|^{q_e}\wedge L)\,dQ(u)le M_e.
 \tag{11}
\]
The strict inequality \(q_e>1\) is used in the uniform-integrability bound
\[
 \sup_m\int_{|u|>R}|u|\,dQ_m(u)
 \le M_eR^{1-q_e}\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{12}
\]
and the same bound holds for \(Q\) by (11).  Apply (10) to the identity
clipped to \([-R,R]\), use (12), and let \(R\to\infty\).  This proves
\(\int u\,dQ_m(u)\to\int u\,dQ(u)\), so the centering restriction on
\(Q_2\) is closed.

The same moment condition automatically supplies the protected frequency
neighborhood that was formerly imposed separately.  By H\"older's inequality,
\[
 \int |u|\,dQ_m(u)
 \le\left\{\int |u|^{q_e}\,dQ_m(u)\right\}^{1/q_e}
 \le M_e^{1/q_e}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Consequently
\[
 |\phi_{Q_m}(s)-\phi_{Q_m}(t)|
 \le\int |e^{isu}-e^{itu}|\,dQ_m(u)
 \le |s-t|M_e^{1/q_e}.
 \tag{14}
\]
Since \(\phi_{Q_m}(0)=1\), the reverse triangle inequality also gives
\[
 |\phi_{Q_m}(t)|
 \ge 1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\ge\frac12
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 |t|\le\nu_*:=\frac{1}{2M_e^{1/q_e}}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Equations (11), (13)--(15) apply to the limit \(Q\) as well.  Weak convergence
in (10) gives pointwise convergence of characteristic functions, and the
common Lipschitz modulus (14), applied on a finite frequency mesh, upgrades it
to uniform convergence on every compact frequency interval.  Thus the moment
ball, with centering imposed for the second coordinate, is sequentially
compact and closed in the weak topology.  In any metric inducing that
topology, sequential compactness implies compactness: otherwise one could
construct either an infinite uniformly separated sequence or a Cauchy
sequence with no limit, each contradicting the convergent-subsequence
property.  This proves compactness of both error-law coordinate sets.  Notice
that (15) derives, rather than assumes, a uniform nonvanishing neighborhood.

Finite products of the compact mass, signal, and error-law coordinate sets are
compact, and all defining cross-coordinate inequalities were shown closed.
Therefore \(\mathscr K\) is compact in the stated product topology.

Let \(\vartheta_m\to\vartheta\) in this topology.  Common compact support and
uniform signal convergence give
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathbb R}
 |\widehat f_{x,m}(r)-\widehat f_x(r)|
 \le 2B_A\|f_{x,m}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{16}
\]
and the same inequality holds with \(q_x\) in place of \(f_x\).  The locally
uniform characteristic-function convergence proved after (15), the bound
\(|\phi_{Q_j}|\le1\), and
\(\int|q_x|\le B_Y\int f_x=B_Y\) show that the fitted channels
\[
 (s,t)\longmapsto
 \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t),
 \qquad
 (s,t)\longmapsto
 \widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)
 \tag{17}
\]
converge locally uniformly on \(\mathbb R^2\).

For continuity of the profiled target, let \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\in\mathscr K\).
On \(I\), the denominator bounds \(f_x,f'_x\ge\kappa\) and domination
\(|q'_x|\le B_Yf'_x\) imply
\[
 \left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q'_x}{f'_x}\right\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le \kappa^{-1}\|q_x-q'_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
     +B_Y\kappa^{-1}\|f_x-f'_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Also \(\|q'_x/f'_x\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le B_Y\).  Therefore
\[
 \|\mu_\vartheta-\mu_{\vartheta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le \sum_xp_x
 \left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q'_x}{f'_x}\right\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 +B_Y\sum_x|p_x-p'_x|,
 \tag{19}
\]
which tends to zero with the product distance.  Thus
\(\vartheta\mapsto\mu_\vartheta\) is continuous into \(C(I)\).

Finally, fix \(n\) and a realized sample \(z\).  Under
\(\textnormal{def:exact-joint-feasible-set}\), define the probability-channel
violation
\[
 v^F_{x,s,t}(z,\vartheta)=
 \left(
 \left|\widehat F_{x,n}(z;s,t)-
 \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)\right|
 -\rho^F_{x,n}(z)
 \right)_+,
 \tag{20}
\]
define \(v^G_{x,s,t}\) analogously, and define the mass violation from
\(\textnormal{def:mass-confidence-region}\) by
\[
 v^p_x(z,\vartheta)=
 \left(
 |p_x-\widehat p_x(z)|-
 \left\{\frac{\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}
 \right)_+.
 \tag{21}
\]
There are finitely many such functions because \(\mathcal X\) and
\(\mathcal D_n\) are finite by \(\textnormal{def:upper-tuning-grid}\).
The empirical sums, counts, empty-cell convention, and radii from
\(\textnormal{def:ecf-radii}\) are Borel measurable in \(z\), so
(20)--(21) are measurable in \(z\).  Equation (17) and continuity of the mass
coordinates show that they are continuous in \(\vartheta\).  Their common
zero set is exactly \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\).  It is closed in
the compact space \(\mathscr K\), and therefore compact.  This proves every
assertion of the lemma under the enlarged ranges.

proposed.name: \(\mathscr K\)
proposed.construction:
Fix \(\beta>1/2\) and \(q_e>1\).  For a Borel probability law \(Q_j\) on
\(\mathbb R\), put
\(\phi_{Q_j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{itu}\,dQ_j(u)\).  The exact projected
nuisance class \(\mathscr K\) is the set of tuples
\[
 \vartheta=\bigl((p_x,f_x,q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X},Q_1,Q_2\bigr)
\]
such that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 p_x\ge p_{\min}\quad(x\in\mathcal X),\qquad
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x=1,\\
 f_x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R,\quad f_x\in H^\beta(\mathbb R),\quad f_x\ge0,
 \quad \int_{\mathbb R}f_x(a)\,da=1,\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(f_x)\subseteq\mathcal A,\\
 \|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\le R_f,qquad
 \inf_{a\in I}f_x(a)\ge\kappa,\\
 q_x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R,\quad q_x\in H^\beta(\mathbb R),\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(q_x)\subseteq\mathcal A,\quad
 \|q_x\|_{H^\beta}\le R_q,\\
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\quad(a\in\mathbb R),\\
 \int_{\mathbb R}|u|^{q_e}\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e\quad(j=1,2),\qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}u\,dQ_2(u)=0.
 \end{gathered}
\]
No separate lower-modulus restriction is imposed on either error
characteristic function.  All pointwise signal constraints use the continuous
representatives supplied by \(\beta>1/2\).  The tuple represents the product
error law \(Q_1\otimes Q_2\); it is an outer projection of the full causal
class and does not assert that every one of its elements has a structural
causal realization.  For \(a\in I\), define
\[
 \mu_\vartheta(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact projected class must share the enlarged model ranges \(\beta>1/2\) and \(q_e>1\), and the moment radius itself yields a uniform protected characteristic-function neighborhood, so retaining \(\nu_0\) and \(c_0\) would impose a redundant smaller class.
